quest.title: The Legend of the Mysterious Island
quest.description: Your curiosity having been piqued, you decide to head to the People of the Springs, and ask the tribal leader about the legends of the mysterious island.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x325, Mora x27825, Amina's Compensation x1, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: Where the Springs Return: Act II
chapter.title: The Legend of the Mysterious Island

talks.objective: Look for the People of the Springs's chief

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: So what brings you here? Do you need help with anything?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We want to visit the mysterious island!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: The mysterious island, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, is there something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I'm assuming you two are already aware that this island is related to a legend of my people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, but now that you mention it, we don't know anything about the actual legend yet.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Then allow me to explain it to you two.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: It is said that the first chief of the People of the Springs was the most outstanding guide in all of Natlan. He discovered many deserted domains and found countless treasures.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: But to prove himself once more, he embarked on yet another journey, in search of a legendary mysterious island. He endured many hardships along the way, but he persevered and managed to reach the destination.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: The island emits a golden light, where countless treasures are buried. But instead of claiming the treasures for himself, he left behind a trail of clues that lead to the island.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Since then, many people from later generations have undertaken the challenge of finding the island. After all, to find the island is to find riches and glory.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that makes sense! So could you tell us how to get to that island?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it. This is a big secret for the People of the Springs, so you can't just tell anyone, right?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: On the contrary, it's quite the opposite. The legend and the clues needed to find the island are all already known to the public.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Well, then what's the problem?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Well, I'm willing to answer your question in exchange for a favor. What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sure thing, but what do you need us to do?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Then you have my thanks. Allow me to tell you some details.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I'll be honest, there are some among the tribe who are of rather base character. Not long ago, I received a report that a few of them were working together to scam visitors.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: As the chief of the tribe, I was very ashamed to hear of this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's really hard to believe that could happen!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: They are targeting tourists who wish to visit that island.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: According to my sources, they would trick tourists into believing they are trustworthy guides, before luring the tourists into spending a fortune for the sake of reaching the island.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: They run a pretty sophisticated operation. They would always claim the scammed money as some kind of legal travel expenditure, so it's hard to use that to directly convict them.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: So, I was hoping to find someone who could approach them and pretend to get scammed. Doing so would allow us to gather the evidence required to bring them to justice.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: The problem is... They would certainly recognize anyone associated with me, which is why I haven't been able to carry out the plan yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon understands now. We're the perfect bait because we're both tourists!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Exactly. And as far as I know, you two are no pushovers. No matter what nefarious schemes they may come up with, you'll be perfectly capable of protecting yourselves, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #You betcha! If it's just a few scammers we're talking about, {M#he}{F#she} will take 'em all down!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Wonderful. Then here, please take this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that's a lot of Mora! Did we already earn a bonus?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: There will be plenty of rewards if you manage to catch those scoundrels. This Mora, however, is for other purposes.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I'm sure some spending will be required on your part before they lower their guard. I certainly wouldn't expect you to pay out of your own pockets.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: So please use the Mora as needed, and collect as much evidence as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wonder you're the chief! Seems like you've already thought of everything. Okay, we'll take it from here!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I've marked the location of the scammers on your map. I'll leave the rest to you two.

talks.objective: Go to the designated location to lure the scammer out

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should be the place! Now, let's see if anyone around here looks like a scammer!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right, we should pretend we are innocent tourists with no idea about what's going on! But how should we lure those scammers out?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe try talking about the mysterious island?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good idea. Speaking of which, Paimon's dying to know what kind of treasures could be buried on the mysterious island! Wonder if anyone's ever really seen them before!

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Ah, are you two visitors from afar looking to visit the mysterious island?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who the...? Oh, looks like we managed to lure them out already.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: C'mon, Paimon, don't forget our roles.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem... Oh, pardon, is something the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: I just happened to overhear you two talking about the mysterious island. I assume you two must be tourists brought here by the legend and looking for the island, am I right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hello, Paimon is Paimon, and this is {NICKNAME}. That's right, we were just getting ready to look for that island from the legend!

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: In that case, as a qualified guide, I certainly cannot allow you to embark on such a dangerous journey.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: As the legend says, if you can manage to reach the mysterious island, riches and glory will be yours for the taking.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Be that as it may, the journey to the island is full of untold perils and dangers. It would be nigh impossible for any average person to reach the island.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: But you are in luck! Allow me to tell you the purpose of our services. It just so happens that our mission as guides is to help visitors avoid danger, find shortcuts, and successfully reach their destination.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, this was all a pitch for your services?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Please, there's no need to worry. This was just one point I had to make perfectly clear.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Although the legend and the clues to finding the island are known to everyone, the leads left behind by our ancestors are as enigmatic as riddles found on a lost treasure map.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Only guides bestowed with the legacy of our ancestors can correctly decipher the clues. Tourists who rashly embark on their own often wind up lost and encounter unnecessary dangers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, he actually sounds pretty convincing...

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: But it seems like fate has brought us together, so what say you to having me as your guide?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, so how much will you charge us?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Not to worry, I don't intend to charge any fees.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you'd be working for... free?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: For us People of the Springs, guiding guests to the mysterious island is a great honor in of itself, worth more than any amount of Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Smooth, Paimon almost wants to believe him...

choices.text: This is all still a part of his sales pitch.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, thank you. Then please, guide us onward!

choices.text: We need to see what he actually wants to do.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeho
dialogues.text: Hmm? Are you two here to take pictures with the Koholasaurs?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really, can we!?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Ahem...!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeho
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh... You two must be here to seek insight from Ata, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, Ata? Insight?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeho
dialogues.text: Shh, not so loud. Openly saying their name in such a manner will only cause them to loathe you.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Ah, I apologize for not explaining earlier. As you can see, Ata is the elder Koholasaur my senior here is responsible to serve.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Ata is highly respected among the tribe, and is far more knowledgeable than other Koholasaurs. They say that Ata has actually visited the mysterious island before.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Therefore, we must rely on Ata's insight to know how to get there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? But how do we do that? Can a Koholasaurus elder talk?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: You need only slowly approach Ata. Once Ata has confirmed your scent, they will provide their wise insight... In the language of the Koholasaurs, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: But no need to worry. The ability to interpret this language is one of the basic skills required of a guide from the People of the Springs.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: I can understand Ata's instructions, and will lead you on the journey ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright... then let's give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeho
dialogues.text: Ahem! That'll be 10,000 Mora per person.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeho
dialogues.text: Uh, in order for Ata to give us insight, they must recall their past, which can be extremely taxing for a Koholasaur. Costs to maintain their health can be quite high, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, such expenses may arise in the process of finding our way. But as long as we reach the mysterious island, these costs will be quite trivial in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you have it... Paimon knew there was no such thing as a free lunch.

choices.text: Just pay up. Let's not make him suspicious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon has an idea! She bets they've just made up all that stuff about the talking Koholasaur. But if we can get a receipt, that'll be proof that they're scamming tourists.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: With that kind of evidence, there'd be no doubt that they're guilty.

response.speaker: Kaeho
response.text: What's taking them so long... Well, what do you say? I'll even throw in a group photo of you two with Ata. You won't ever find another deal like this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's an unexpected bonus! Quick, let's pay the man!

choices.text: It should also help us gather evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this where the chief of the People of the Springs should be?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: #Someone looking for me? Oh, why, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and {M#his}{F#her} companion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So the chief's a... little kid? And wait, how do you already know us?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: As chief of the tribe, I must stay informed about everything that could have a significant impact on Natlan. That way, I can come up with the best possible plans for the tribe.

talks.objective: Try to get closer to Ata and take a photo together

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, Ata really didn't try to bite us at all!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeho
dialogues.text: You can also pose now if you'd like a photo together.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay!

dialogues.speaker: Ata
dialogues.text: (Ata makes a noise, but it's hard to tell the meaning.)

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Oh, Ata is already speaking! Let me listen to what they have to say... Oh, I see!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could you really get anything from that noise?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Of course. Like I said, only a guide like me can understand their language. Let's follow Ata's instructions and proceed to the next area.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeho
dialogues.text: Here's your group photo. I even packaged it up for free.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Any chance we could get a receipt for that?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeho
dialogues.text: No problem at all. Here ya go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hee-hee!

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Please, come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We still have a lot of the chief's Mora to use. Why don't we keep up the act and gather some more evidence?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good idea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh, Paimon's curious what other tricks these scammers are using.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Under Kaulu's guidance, you obtain one "clue" after another while forking over Mora left and right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These guys are going way too far! He keeps coming up with some far-fetched reasons to make us pay for everything!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: With all the evidence we have now, we could bring him straight to the chief and he'd definitely be convicted!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, after handing over all that Mora, Paimon kinda wants to see if he'll actually take us to the island or not.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It wouldn't hurt to gather some more evidence.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Sorry to keep you waiting. After all the clues we've gathered, I've managed to find a shortcut to the island!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, alright. Then let's get going!

talks.objective: Follow the directions to the designated location

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: This is the spot. The trails of sunlight will guide the way. Once you cross the rushing water, the light of the setting sun shall reveal everything.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Ata's insights have already pointed us to the destination. It's just on the opposite bank!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean we're almost there? Huh, but there wasn't even anything exciting about this journey...

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: As I said before, this is a shortcut. If I took you on some arduous path after all the Mora you spent, that wouldn't make me look like a good guide, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Anyway, there's no time to lose. We need to get there before sunset.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! We can go find Mualani!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: It appears you've already made up your minds. Then I'll be taking my leave. My assistants will pay you for all your help. Thanks again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, bye-bye!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Paimon has a good feeling about this. Then let's go check out some of the other places first!

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: According to Ata's insights, this is the place. We're here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean the mysterious island...?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Yes, I've led you to the island just as I promised, which means it's time for me to say goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hold on, are you serious!? This is supposed to be the island!? Then what about the treasure? And look at these wooden signs and artificial lights. Even we can tell it's fake!

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: All that stuff about treasure is just part of the legend — I didn't make any promises about what you'd find. And who says a mysterious island can't look like this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph, since you seem to have dropped the act, then there's no need for us to continue, either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were commissioned by the chief of the People of the Springs to gather evidence of your scamming activities! With these receipts, your scamming days are over.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Heh, you sure? Then what's written on those receipts?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... Huh? Wait, all the writing has disappeared!?

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: I took you all this way just to buy enough time for the handwriting to disappear. Even if you were to go back to the people you paid, you'd only find that they were using fake names, making them impossible to track down.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: You wanna report me for scamming tourists, then be my guest. I'll just say that I'm being falsely accused. With that settled, I'll be going now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, now he's trying to get away! Let's go after him!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You go chasing after Kaulu, but soon find that he's been stopped by a group of people from his tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's the chief!

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: What's the chief doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I had dispatched others to secretly trail you. Thanks to you, we can finally convict him of scamming people.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Convict me? How? They don't have any evidence against me. Even as the chief, you can't just level accusations without any evidence, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry to say it, but he got us. We lost all the evidence we had...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Not to worry, let's search him first.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Hey, what are you doing? Keep your hands off me, that's my Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Yes, I see the mark... Looks like you already split the Mora before you led them here.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: #The Mora that {NICKNAME} and Paimon were using today were all provided by me. They all have a special mark on them.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: You...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: So, there must be an explanation why the Mora that should have been theirs ended up in your hands, right?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: There are no receipts to prove that any transactions took place, and you yourself just denied that there was a scam... So did you, then, take the Mora from them by force?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Take Mora from others by force!? Oh, that's an even more serious crime than scamming!

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Ah, y—you... Ugh, alright. Sure, I admit that I coaxed them into spending a few times... But I wouldn't go as far as calling it "scamming"...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: We have witnesses standing right here, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Fine... Yes, it was all a scam.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woohoo! No wonder you're the chief of the tribe!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I still don't understand how so many people have been getting duped by them. You need only stop and think for a moment to see through the whole thing.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: If he claims to be able to find a shortcut to the mysterious island, then why hasn't he just gone there and claimed the treasure for himself? Why even bother guiding others there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a good point. Speaking of, have any guides from the People of the Springs ever found the treasure of the mysterious island?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: I can answer this question along with your previous one about how to get there. The answer is actually very simple—

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: There is no shortcut to the island, and most people don't even meet the requirement to ever reach it.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: If you don't meet this single condition, then even guides from the People of the Springs, despite all of their abilities, will find it difficult to overcome the obstacles along the way...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Which is exactly why even though the clues to the mysterious island are open to the public, few have ever made it there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a requirement? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Let me ask you something first. What do you think a real journey to the mysterious island should be like?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, it should probably involve... overcoming a lot of hardships with your companions, before witnessing some breathtaking sights, uncovering a really touching story... Oh! And scoring some super cool treasure at the end!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: And therein lies the key point... overcoming hardships with your companions.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: It's said that when the first chief set out to search for the island, the ones who accompanied him were not clients, nor tourists, but his closest friends.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: The legend also mentioned that only those willing to entrust their lives to one another will be able to reach the island together.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Therefore, the requirement to reach the island is journeying with your closest friends... The kind of friends you would trust with your life.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's the key...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: From what I can see, you and Paimon are exactly those kinds of friends, the kind that would trust each other with anything.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: But unfortunately, neither of you are experienced guides. And if you were to hire someone else, then I'm afraid you could probably never place your lives in the hands of someone you met on a pure monetary basis.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: But don't feel discouraged! I believe that this beautiful land that I call my home will not disappoint you.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Whether it's remote islands or ancient ruins, I'm sure they can also provide you with plenty of exciting adventures.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: And let me tell you a secret. The elders once told me that beneath these very ruins lies a way to reach the sky!

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Or, maybe somebody already discovered that...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: No matter, if you two want to go adventuring elsewhere, I can also give you some suggestions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, thanks for that! But knowing us, we don't give up so easily, even when a place is supposedly "impossible" to visit...

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Oh, I can understand. I won't stop you if you're still interested in finding the island. I just recommend finding a guide first who you could trust with your lives.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A guide we could trust with our lives? Who knows when we'll meet someone like that around here...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe it won't take as long as you think.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: #Someone looking for me? Oh, why, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and {M#his}{F#her} companion.

dialogues.speaker: Amina
dialogues.text: Please remember, we need concrete evidence. I'm counting on you.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeho
dialogues.text: Remember, approach them slowly. You don't want to scare Ata.

dialogues.speaker: Kaulu
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I will help interpret Ata's insights.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeho
dialogues.text: Didn't I tell you not to scare Ata!? *sigh* Let me calm them down, and you can try again.
